speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our investigation, have these symptoms been present for more than a few weeks, and have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the combination of "drenching" night sweats, significant weight loss (12 lbs), and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy suggests a serious underlying condition. Given your abdominal pain and fatigue, have you noticed any blood in your stool, black tarry stools, or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gastric Lymphoma (MALT lymphoma) secondary to chronic H. pylori infection.

While the patient's history of a prior "Tuberculosis" diagnosis and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are concerning for malignancy, the specific combination of four weeks of abdominal pain, significant weight loss, night sweats, and fixed lymph node swelling is highly suggestive of a lymphoproliferative disorder involving the gastrointestinal tract.

REQUEST TEST: H. pylori stool antigen test, Upper Endoscopy with biopsy, and CT Abdomen/Pelvis.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis showing lymphadenopathy and gastric wall thickening.
